vectors.text: I'm Ajaykumar Balakannan — most people call me Ajay. I'm a data scientist based in Dallas, TX, finishing a Master's in Data Science at the University of Maryland (expected May 2026, GPA 3.74/4.0). I've built production ML, NLP, and LLM-orchestrated systems over large operational and workforce datasets — anomaly detection on 15M+ job-market records, a no-show prediction model that reroutes counseling appointments, salary models across 40,000+ US zip codes. The through-line is that I like owning the whole path: the ingestion pipeline, the model, and the dashboard someone actually opens on Monday morning. I'm looking for full-time data science, ML engineering, and analytics roles.

vectors.text: How I work, in my own words: I build end-to-end rather than handing off a notebook. At Maryland that meant the DuckDB pipeline, the LightGBM model, and the Tableau dashboard the counseling staff use — all of it, because a model nobody can act on isn't finished. I care a lot about whether the thing gets adopted; the numbers I'm proudest of are adoption numbers (25% better resource utilization, 60% less manual reporting, 15+ analyst hours saved a week) rather than leaderboard scores. I reach for explainability by default — SHAP on the no-show model, so the counseling team could see why someone was flagged and trust it. I'm suspicious of my own data: I ran PyOD and Cleanlab validation across Canaria's 15M+ records specifically to catch what the pipeline was quietly getting wrong. And I like measuring claims instead of asserting them — for TravelGenie I load-tested EC2 against ECS Fargate at 50-100 concurrent users rather than guessing which was cheaper. I'd rather ship something small that works than something elaborate that demos well.

My timeline, so the dates line up. Aug 2020 - May 2024: B.Tech in Electrical and Electronics Engineering at Sri Krishna College of Engineering and Technology, Coimbatore, India. Mar 2023 - Jul 2024: Data & Analytics Engineer at AastraZen Technologies in Chennai — this overlapped my final year of the B.Tech and continued a couple of months past graduation. Sep 2024 - present: Data Scientist at the University of Maryland Counseling Center, College Park, alongside my Master's. May 2025 - Aug 2025: Data Science Intern at Canaria Inc. in New York — that was the summer of 2025, which is the summer before last relative to late 2026, and the most recent full-time summer role I've held. Expected May 2026: Master's in Data Science, University of Maryland. As of August 2026 I'm still at the UMD Counseling Center, based in Dallas, TX, and looking for full-time roles.

I'm doing my Master's in Data Science at the University of Maryland, College Park, expected May 2026, with a GPA of 3.74/4.0 (an earlier-term internal document lists 3.78/4.0). Coursework that mattered most: Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Big Data Systems, and Deep Learning. Maryland is a large public R1 university in College Park, just outside Washington, DC, and several of my NLP and deep-learning course projects — the RNN comparison, the n-gram modeling work, the gun-violence coverage analysis — came out of that program.

vectors.text: My undergraduate degree is a B.Tech in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from Sri Krishna College of Engineering and Technology (SKCET) in Coimbatore, India, Aug 2020 - May 2024, CGPA 8.4/10.0. SKCET is an autonomous private engineering institution founded in 1998, affiliated with Anna University, with NBA-accredited programs and a place in the NIRF engineering top 100. Relevant coursework: Microcontrollers, Power System Analysis, Python, and Machine Learning in Energy Systems. Coming from electrical engineering rather than computer science is part of why I gravitate toward systems that touch the physical world — the farmland detection project was hardware plus vision, not just a model.

Since Sep 2024 I've been a Data Scientist at the University of Maryland Counseling Center in College Park, working alongside my Master's. The Counseling Center is the university's mental-health service for students, so everything I build there touches appointment access and staff time. I built a no-show prediction model — Random Forest plus LightGBM, with SHAP for explainability — on student counseling appointment records; it triggers automated outreach and lifted resource utilization by 25%. I used Sentence-Transformers (SetFit) and BERTopic to classify 4,000+ pieces of student feedback from e-forms and audio transcripts, surfacing sentiment and service themes the counseling staff now act on. I engineered Python, DuckDB, and SQL pipelines that ingest 12+ years of operational records into version-controlled data models — that's the backbone under both the models and the KPI reporting. I automated the data-refresh workflows behind Tableau and Power BI dashboards covering utilization, cancellations, and peak demand, cutting manual reporting turnaround by 60%. I also ran hypothesis testing and sentiment analysis on 10+ years of student survey data, which helped administrators secure budget increases two quarters running, and supported resource-allocation discussions that cut redundant resources by 20%.

I was a Data Science Intern at Canaria Inc. in New York from May 2025 to Aug 2025 — the summer of 2025. I built v0 statistical models and v1 PyCaret pipelines (Isolation Forest, KNN, HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM) over 15M+ job-market records, containerized with Docker, which cut false-positive anomaly flags by 35% in production. I developed a salary prediction model (LightGBM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) across 40,000+ US zip codes, segmented by SOC code x location x seniority and experience, wired into an MLflow-tracked, auto-recalibrating ClickHouse pipeline for real-time forecasting and deployed on AWS; it helped bring in 10+ new clients. I ran PyOD and Cleanlab automated validation over the same 15M+ distributed records to catch statistical outliers. I designed Polars and PySpark ingestion pipelines across three cloud systems — ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, and AWS S3 — to keep the job-market data clean for downstream analytics. I also built LLM-powered GenAI workflows over unstructured text that automated summarization and reporting, saving 15+ analyst hours a week.

About Canaria Inc., where I interned in summer 2025: Canaria is a New York-based job-market data startup founded in 2022. It sells research-grade labor-market intelligence — on the order of a billion deduplicated job postings enriched with 100+ fields, SOC occupation codes, salary signals, and a taxonomy of 40,000+ skills — plus company profiles and AI-extracted compensation data, to customers in HR, recruitment, workforce analytics, and financial modeling. That context explains the shape of my work there: when your product is a labor-market dataset, a bad posting or a mis-scored salary is a defect that ships to clients, which is why so much of my internship was anomaly detection, validation, and recalibration rather than modeling for its own sake.

From Mar 2023 to Jul 2024 I was a Data & Analytics Engineer at AastraZen Technologies in Chennai, India — this overlapped my final year of undergrad and ran a couple of months past graduation. I fine-tuned a Hugging Face DistilBERT model for automated support-ticket categorization and built a semantic search feature on a vector database, cutting manual ticket triage time by 45% across client support workflows. I migrated a legacy client database to a hybrid MongoDB + PostgreSQL architecture with dbt-managed transformation layers, improving query throughput by 40% and enabling real-time reporting for a mid-market client. And I architected a real-time streaming pipeline on Apache Kafka feeding a centralized AWS S3 data lake, supporting concurrent analytics workloads across 5+ client accounts at 99.5% uptime. This was the job where I learned data engineering properly — most of what I know about pipelines holding up in production came from here.

About AastraZen Technologies, where I worked from Mar 2023 to Jul 2024: it's a private software services company incorporated in March 2019 and based in Sholinganallur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu. It does software development services and IT corporate training, and sells SaaS customer-engagement tooling that support, sales, and marketing teams use to communicate with their customers. Because it's a services company working across multiple client accounts rather than a single product team, I ended up touching a wide spread of stacks — support-ticket NLP for one client, a database migration for another, Kafka streaming shared across several — which is how I got breadth early.

My technical stack. AI and machine learning: LLM orchestration (Claude, MCP), generative AI, LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, Isolation Forest, ARIMA, SetFit, BERTopic, DistilBERT, scikit-learn, PyCaret, HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, SVM. Data platforms and warehousing: Snowflake, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, Databricks, Redshift, MongoDB, DuckDB, AWS (S3, EC2), MLflow, dbt, Kafka. Languages and processing: Python, SQL, R, Pandas, NumPy, Polars, PySpark, PyOD, Cleanlab, MATLAB. Visualization and reporting: Tableau, Power BI, Qlik Sense, Sigma, Quarto and Jupyter, KPI tracking, root cause analysis. Data engineering and cloud: Docker, Apache Spark, Hadoop, Azure, Git and CI/CD, relational data modeling. If you want the short version: Python and SQL are the daily drivers, LightGBM is my default first model on tabular problems, and I'm comfortable owning the AWS and pipeline side rather than treating it as someone else's job.

TravelGenie is my AI travel planning system, built Dec 2025 — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/TravelGenie. It plans a trip by coordinating flights, hotels, events, weather, currency, and traffic data through one request instead of ten browser tabs. The architecture is seven standalone MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers — Flight, Hotel, Event, Geocoder, Weather, Finance, and Traffic & Crowd — each doing exactly one job, with Claude orchestrating and chaining their outputs: geocode a location, then search flights and hotels near it, then check the weather for those dates. Flight, hotel, and event data comes from SerpAPI; Open-Meteo and OpenStreetMap need no API key. It ships as a Streamlit web UI and a Slack bot, and the MCP servers can also run directly inside Claude Desktop. It deploys via Docker or AWS (ECS Fargate, DynamoDB, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch, provisioned with CloudFormation). The part I'd point at: I benchmarked EC2 against ECS Fargate under sustained and stress load with 50-100 concurrent users, and Fargate matched EC2's 460 RPS on roughly half the compute. MIT licensed.

vectors.text: Farmland wildlife intrusion detection, Mar 2023 — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Framland_Protection. It's an AI-driven, non-lethal alternative to electric fencing and chemical repellents for keeping wildlife off farmland. A camera monitors the field continuously; YOLOv3 does real-time animal detection at around 90% accuracy with non-maximum suppression to drop redundant boxes; a second validation stage — a CNN for species verification plus a Random Forest to filter false positives — cuts false alarms by about 40%; a confirmed detection then triggers an Arduino controller that fires a deterrent matched to the animal (sound for nocturnal animals, light for herbivores like deer, water sprinklers for medium-sized animals). Every detection is logged with image, species, time, and location for conservation and census use. One honest correction: the README's 'want to improve' section lists upgrading to YOLOv5 as future work — YOLOv3 is what I actually implemented and demoed, even though a couple of later materials (a portfolio tag, one resume version) say YOLOv5. It won 2nd place among 500+ teams and a $300 prize at the National Technocraft Hackathon (Technocraft Booth Project Competition 2022-23, held at COEP, Pune, 2nd May 2023), and the work was published in BIOGECKO (Vol 12, Issue 03, 2023). We built and tested a hardware prototype alongside the software pipeline.

Bitcoin price forecasting, 2025 — a Qlik Sense project under causify-ai/tutorials (TutorTask146). End-to-end: live BTC price collection, ARIMA and XGBoost forecasting models at around 85% predictive accuracy, automated ingestion/validation/transformation workflows, and interactive Qlik Sense dashboards giving real-time visibility into volatility and market drivers. It cut manual reporting effort by about 40%.

vectors.text: Sage Ventures multifamily real estate analytics pipeline, 2025 — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/RealEstateModelling. Being straight about this one: it's a self-built portfolio demonstration project, not client work. I simulated the data infrastructure, reporting, and BI of a multifamily real estate portfolio to demonstrate SQL, Python, Power BI, and Excel skills for a junior data-analyst-type role, and the underlying data is synthetic, generated with Faker. Sage Ventures itself is a real firm — a Baltimore/Pikesville, Maryland real estate company founded in 2004 that acquires, develops, rehabilitates, and manages multifamily properties across the DC-Baltimore region — which is what I modeled the scenario on. The pipeline runs in one command (run_pipeline.py) across five phases: generate_data.py builds a SQLite DB and raw CSVs; feature_engineering.py creates 15+ engineered features; adhoc_analysis.py produces 5 business reports; excel_report.py builds a 7-sheet workbook; visualize.py generates 10 charts. Data model: properties to units to tenants to rent_roll, plus properties to maintenance and properties to occupancy_monthly. Stack: Python, SQLite, SQL, Pandas, openpyxl, Matplotlib, Power BI. Illustrative findings from the simulated portfolio: 67% average occupancy against a 93% target, $2.14M annual loss-to-lease, $19,864 in delinquency exposure, and 533 open maintenance tickets past SLA.

The CANARIA Anomaly Detection System — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Version-1-anomaly — is the job-market anomaly detection work tied to my Canaria internship. It finds unusual patterns in job posting data at three granularities: US level (geo_level x source), state level (state x source), and SOC/occupation level (SOC code x source). Parquet files are read in configurable batches (default 50,000 rows), cleaned and validated, then stored in MongoDB under a rolling window (default 45 days) so the models keep adapting to recent data without storage growing without bound. Feature engineering generates 18 features per record: rolling statistics over 7/14/28 days, temporal features (day-of-week, week, month), statistical measures (z-scores, MAD), and expanding-window long-term patterns. The model layer is a 7-model ensemble — PyCaret's Isolation Forest, KNN, and SVM, plus PyOD's HBOS, COPOD, OCSVM, and CBLOF — with scores averaged for robustness and compared against per-segment quantile thresholds, with cooldown logic so it doesn't spam alerts. Output is CSV results with scores, plus logging and performance monitoring.

Resume Optimiser and Outreach Automation — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Resume_Optimiser — is two tools in one repo, and it's the thing I'm actively building right now. First, a resume optimizer CLI (resume_api.py): paste in a job description and get back a tailored one-page LaTeX resume, a cover-letter paragraph, and an email draft, generated through the Claude API and compiled with pdflatex. Second, an outreach web app in Next.js: upload a contacts CSV, attach a resume, write one email template, preview every personalized message, and send the batch through Gmail via OAuth. It integrates with Apollo.io to find and reveal contacts at a target company (leadership and role-matched tiers) and writes a bespoke AI-personalized paragraph per contact using Claude Haiku plus a free web-search cascade (Tavily, Exa, Brave) for real context on each person — with guardrails that reject generic-AI-sounding phrasing or a too-casual tone and retry with a correction. Cost and usage are tracked per call (tokens, cache hits, USD) and surfaced in an analytics view, because I wanted to actually know what the thing costs to run.

BudgetPlay — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/BudgetPlay — is a participatory budgeting simulator I built for an Anthropic Hackathon (Track #3: Governance & Accessibility). You explore how a city-sized budget is allocated, move sliders to rebalance spending across categories, read a Claude-generated plain-language narrative explaining the tradeoffs of your reallocation, and optionally submit your budget as a 'vote' grouped by region. A companion 'Government Pulse' dashboard aggregates submissions so community averages can be compared against the official budget, with percentage-point shifts by category and short recommendation blurbs. Stack: Node.js and Express on the backend, a static frontend (Tailwind, Chart.js, vanilla JS), and the Anthropic Messages API for the impact-narrative endpoint. The budget data is explicitly sample and educational — not a real government budget.

A comparative analysis of RNN architectures for sentiment classification, from my UMD coursework — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Sentiment-Analysis. I implemented and compared plain RNN, LSTM, and Bidirectional LSTM on the IMDb movie review dataset, varying activation functions (sigmoid, ReLU, tanh), optimizers (Adam, SGD, RMSprop), sequence lengths (25/50/100 words), and gradient clipping on and off, to see how each choice moves sentiment classification performance.

N-gram language modeling and evaluation, UMD coursework — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/N_Gram_Modelling. I implemented and evaluated Maximum Likelihood Estimation n-gram language models, unigram through 4-gram, on the Penn Treebank dataset, looking at the trade-off between n-gram order and the role of smoothing and backoff in handling data sparsity, with perplexity evaluation and text generation.

A comparative analysis of gun violence coverage across news outlets, from my UMD NLP coursework — github.com/AjaykumarBalakannan/Comparative_Analysis_HW5. I used NLP techniques including coreference resolution via spaCy to analyze how CNN, Fox News, The New York Times, and The Wall Street Journal portray victims and shooters across gun violence incidents, over a dataset of 100 articles, 25 per outlet.

My team took 2nd place among 500+ teams and a $300 prize at the National Technocraft Hackathon (Technocraft Booth Project Competition 2022-23, hosted by the Alumni Association of the College of Engineering Pune and the COEP Charitable Foundation USA, held 2nd May 2023) for the farmland wildlife intrusion detection project. It was a team project during my B.Tech at Sri Krishna College of Engineering and Technology. The findings were later published in BIOGECKO, Vol 12, Issue 03, 2023 — a New Zealand biology journal — on YOLO-based AI detection with automated deterrents.

I attended 'PRAYATNA', a 2-day hands-on workshop run by Microsoft and Walmart at IIT Chennai in May 2022, on web and app development — HTML/CSS, JavaScript, responsive design. And I did a web development internship / industrial project at Denshi Solutions in Erode, India, 04/04/2023 to 05/06/2023, as part of a 9-student team from Sri Krishna College's final-year Electrical and Electronics Engineering program, contributing to product development and the web build-out.
